evidence.quote: We note that this assumes that all the dust contributing to the 1.2 mm continuum is heated by hot stars and not by the quasar.

method.value: Mean L_FIR of four CFHQS quasars (J2329 set to 2sigma limit 60 uJy) compared with Herschel-based low-z samples at L_Bol ~7e12 Lsun

method.value: Single power-law fit to 12 z>5 sources with MCMC including observational uncertainties

evidence.quote: We fit the 12 $z>5$ sources with a single power-law model of the dependence of $L_{\rm FIR}$ on $L_{\rm [CII]}$ incorporating the observational (but not systematic) uncertainties using a MCMC procedure.

evidence.loc: Discussion, The [C ii] – far-IR luminosity relation

method.value: FWHM20 = 1.5 FWHM; v_cir=0.75 FWHM/sin i with i=arccos(a_min/a_maj); M_dyn=1.16e5 v_cir^2 D Msun, D=1.5x deconvolved FWHM

evidence.quote: The circular velocity is therefore $v_{\rm cir}=0.75 \,$FWHM$_{\rm [CII]} / \sin i$.
$M_{\rm dyn} \approx 1.16\times 10^5\, v_{\rm cir}^2 \,D \,M_\odot$

key_parameters.value: i=55 deg assumed when unresolved (J2229+1457, J1148, J1120)

evidence.quote: An inclination of $i=55^{\circ}$ is assumed as this is the median inclination angle for the resolved sources in this paper and (cite: Wang:2013).

assumptions.value: [C II] gas in an inclined disk; BH mass uncertainty +0.3 dex (0.45 dex if Eddington-based)

evidence.quote: The \[C ii\] emitting gas is assumed to be in an inclined disk

validation.value: Compared J1148 M_dyn with CO-based literature value

evidence.quote: For comparison (cite: Walter:2004) determined a dynamical mass from CO emission in this quasar of $5.5\times 10^{10}\,M_\odot$

results_numeric.quantity: Mean L_FIR of four CFHQS quasars

evidence.quote: The mean and standard deviation of the sample is $L_{\rm FIR} = (2.6 \pm 1.4) \times 10^{11}\,L_\odot$.

findings_qualitative.value: z=6 CFHQS quasars lie on the local M_BH-sigma relation on average but with much larger scatter.

evidence.quote: whilst there is little mean shift between the $z=0$ and $z\approx 6$ data, there is a much larger scatter in the data at $z\approx 6$

claims.hypothesis: Do z~6 quasars have lower far-IR luminosity (SFR) than luminosity-matched lower-z quasars?
claims.experiment: Compared mean L_FIR of four CFHQS quasars with Herschel-based low-z samples at matched L_Bol
claims.result: Mean L_FIR at z~6 is ~2 lower than z=0.3 and ~6 lower than the z=2.4 peak
claims.finding: z~6 quasars grow black holes faster relative to stellar mass

evidence.quote: The mean $L_{\rm FIR}$ at $z \approx 6$ is a factor of about 2 lower than the $z=0.3$ bin and 6 lower than the $z=2.4$ peak

claims.hypothesis: Are [C II]/FIR ratios of low-L_FIR z>6 quasars like local star-forming galaxies?
claims.experiment: Plotted ratio vs L_FIR with literature samples and fitted z>5 relation
claims.finding: Similar to local galaxies of same L_FIR; shallow negative slope

evidence.quote: The ratios of \[CII\] to far-IR luminosities for the CFHQS quasars lie in the range 0.001 to 0.01

claims.hypothesis: Do lower-mass BH quasars at z~6 lie offset from the local M_BH-sigma relation as selection bias predicts less?
claims.experiment: Derived sigma and M_dyn from [C II] for 10 z>5.7 quasars
claims.result: No significant offset but marked increased scatter, also at 1e8 Msun
claims.finding: Bias hypothesis of lower scatter at low M_BH not supported

evidence.quote: We note that our hypothesis that the bias described in the Introduction would lead to the lower $M_{\rm BH}$ quasars being located on the local relation with a lower scatter than the high $M_{\rm BH}$ quasars is not supported by these observations.

why_this_data.value: Increase sample of ~1e8 Msun BH quasars to test host properties free of the sigma bias

evidence.quote: these quasars are not subject to the bias in the $M_{\rm BH} - \sigma$ relation discussed previously because of their moderate black hole masses

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Low L_FIR could be due to low dust content rather than low SFR; judged not main factor

evidence.quote: However, two lines of evidence point towards this not being the main factor for our quasar sample.

limitations_admitted.value: Dynamical masses highly uncertain (unknown gas structure, marginal resolution, missed extended gas); no formal errors

evidence.quote: We note that there is considerable uncertainty on these values due to the unknown spatial and velocity structure of the gas

limitations_admitted.value: Missing red-wing data of J0055+0146 may bias size and inclination

evidence.quote: We note that the missing data in the red wing of the \[C ii\] line may cause a bias in the size and inclination

referee_caveats_inferred: Tiny sample (4 CFHQS, ~10 total) and heterogeneous literature data
Single-temperature greybody and SFR conversions dominate systematics, not propagated
Assumed inclinations and unresolved sizes drive sigma/M_dyn
